title.narrative: Activity F: Jerusalem Crisis Management: Key stakeholders, decision-makers, and opinion shapers provided with all the information, analyses, and data that they need to: 1) prevent developments that may prejudge or prevent a permanent status agreement in Jerusalem or harm the fragile stability in the city; and 2) mitigate the extreme humanitarian ramifications of occupation.

• Number of persons who read Terrestrial Jerusalem's special analysis and periodical reports and quantity of feedback received. • Number of persons briefed and their seniority. • Type and number of monitored developments deriving from and impacting the conflict between Israelis and Palestinians in Jerusalem. • Number of action alerts sent and number of recipient decision-makers. • Number of detrimental developments prevented that could have further affected Jerusalem stability and the prospect of the two-state solution in Jerusalem. • Number and type of briefings and educational tours to the press and key stakeholders. • Availability of an up-to-date comprehensive database on all matters relating to the conflict in Jerusalem.

target.value: Six (6) reports analysing emerging developments and their ramifications.

Six (6) podcasts.
52 tours.
10 briefings to European diplomats.
Six (6) briefings to senior US officials.
30 inquiries from international officials about information and assessment related to developments in Jerusalem.
Six (6) reports analysing emerging developments and their ramifications, disseminated to 267 subscribers and read by an average of 100 subscribers.
10 updated maps produced illustrating the impact of reported developments.
22.2.k followers on Twitter

actual.value:
11 podcast episodes were produced over the course of 2022.
Terrestiral Jerusalem (TJ) engaged in 16 briefings to senior US officials, 18 briefings to European diplomats and hosted 54 tours for senior decision-makers in the US and European member states. TJ furthermore received 31 inquiries from international officials on a weekly basis requesting information and assessments on various developments in Jerusalem as well as produced 6 reports on emerging developments and their ramifications disseminated to 342 subscribers. 6 updated maps was further created illustrating the impact of developments involving settlement advancement in East Jerusalem. Lastly, TJs Twitter now reached more than 24,000 followers.

target.value: Greater understanding among key stakeholders of the measures needed to address Gaza sources of tensions and long-term challenges. Enhanced support of key stakeholders for a more comprehensice strategy for stabilization. Clearer understanding of the potential contribution of a trilateral approach to Gaza longterm challenges.

actual.value: The activities carried out by Terrestrial Jerusalem (TJ) in 2023 were both shaped and a times overshadowed events in Jerusalem: an Israeli Government unlike anything witnessed before in Israel and the outbreak of the October 7 war. The former issue dominated the dynamics in the first half of 2023, while the October war consumed much of the attention During the first half of 2023, settlement developments in East Jerusalem were taking place in such a frenetic pace that new methods became necessary. In mid-2023, TJ began to produce ongoing and comprehensive reports chronicling those elements of settlement expansion in East Jerusalem that require the urgent attention of the international community. The serious uptick of hate crimes and The aggressive and illegal policing by Ben Gvir’s police in East Jerusalem, along with the spike in home demolitions (also initiated by Ben Gvir) were covered and exposed in TJ’s briefings and reports. Furthermore, the sense of an imminent war was clearly and emphatically articulated by TJ, its staff, and he members of the Jerusalem Policy Task force. Much changed with the outbreak of the war, and some of these changes penetrate to the very core of the conflict between Israelis and Palestinians in general, and in Jerusalem in particular. Consequently, TJ has been compelled to monitor closely as never before; while simultaneously trying to grasp the new dynamics we all are and will be facing in the weeks, months and years to come. TJ conducted numerous briefings for key stakeholders and decision makers in both Israel/Palestine and beyond. TJ also conducted on-going ad hoc discussions with the diplomatic missions in East Jerusalem, Ramallah and Tel Aviv. Some of these took place in the framework of onsite briefing tours in East Jerusalem. (Until October, there was an average of at least one such briefing tour weekly)

title.narrative: Activity C: Enhanced and sustainable Israeli-Palestinian cross-border agricultural cooperation that encourages business-to-business relationships and exchanges on issues of mutual interest and concern.

• Number of opportunities for beneficial cross-border endeavours created through cross-border activities sharing “knowhow.” • Size/scope of agricultural land cultivated in Gaza and West Bank using new knowledge gained through the project. • Number of obstacles to cross-border trade (agricultural and border-crossing related obstacles), addressed/removed.
To be monitored internally by ECF staff by tracking number of cooperative ventures initiated, number of related policy level changes (or benchmarks to changes), Palestinian partners’ reporting and field visits where possible, as well as expert consultants report of receptive dialogue with relevant authorities and other stakeholders.

target.value:
16 seminars to impart skills and knowledge among project participants.
20 professional cross-border study visits facilitating the creation of a tapestry of Israeli-Palestinian agricultural ties.
Three obstacles removed (or benchmarks to removal reached).
600 dunams cultivated with new technologies (implementation & trial).
Israeli authorities and relevant international and Palestinian stakeholders are engaged with ECF in advancing measures to remove obstacles to promote a strengthened Palestinian agricultural sector and enhanced trade capacities in both the West Bank and Gaza.

actual.value:
ECF facilitated 17 activities consisting of seminars imparting skills and knowledge and professional crossborder studies creating tapestry of Israeli-Palestinian agricultural ties, this happened concurrently.
13 obstacles were made vis a vis structural obstacles related to Israeli-controlled crossings and procedures. Other benchmarks for removal of obstacles were reached related to among others import of dual use and fertilizer materials,Gaza herb exports to the US, potential exports of new products from Gaza to Israel, container restrictions and production of tin packages in the Gaza strip for the export of olive oil.
464 dunams of strawberries in the region of Bet Lehia (North Gaza) have been cultivated using IPM.
ECF engaged with as many as 16 Israeli authorities and relevant international and Palestinian stakeholders in order to advance measures to remove obstacles to strengthening the Palestinian agricultural sector and enhanced trade capacities in both the West Bank and Gaza.

target.value: Tapestry of Israel-Palestinian agricultural ties formed, based on cooperation, mutual confidence, and common interests. A strengthened Palestinian agricultural sector and trade capacities, serving as a platform from cross-border cooperation, and to promote economic development in the WB and Gaza.

actual.value: In response to the devastating Gaza war and acknowledging its profound impact on our work in Gaza, ECF strategically redirected our commitment to maintaining and expanding our efforts in the West Bank. During this reporting period, ECF facilitated 14 joint cross-border activities for some 300 agronomists, agro-professionals and heads of local agricultural cooperates in WBG. The events on October 7th, changed the reality for Palestinian farmers from the West Bank significantly. Recognizing the need for tailored support and updated information, ECF has hosted new and revised seminars, along with open discussions including an online meeting between the ECF team, leading Israeli and Palestinian-Israeli farmers and experts from the Israeli Ministry of Agriculture. During this reporting period, progress was made towards the removal of 5 key obstacles: 1. Trade facilitation dialogues and potential follow ups. 2. Monitoring and mitigation of export and crossing obstacles. 3. Addressing challenges in exports through the Israel Ports Authority. 4. Overcoming phytosanitary restrictions for specific Gazan export (mini eggplants/peppers for Israeli pickling industry. 5. Joint meeting on IPM and the pickle industry. ECF engaged with many Israeli authorities and relevant international and Palestinian stakeholders in order to advance measures to remove obstacles to strengthening the Palestinian agricultural sector and enhanced trade capacities. ECF partners made significant progress in implementing advanced agricultural techniques in both the West Bank and Gaza. Efforts to introduce IPM for strawberry crops in Gaza expanded significantly, resulting in ECF-led pilot reaching 804 dunams over several cycles in Beit Lehia.

target.value: Nine (9) cross-border meetings and study visits held providing participants with important networking opportunities.

actual.value: Participation of both Gazan and West Bank farmers in meetings and study visits held at Erez and Sha'ar Efraim crossings, Yad Mordechai and strawberry plots in the Qalansuwa and HaSharon areas. Additionally, we visited the first ("post-Covid") public agricultural exhibition held in October 2021.

title.narrative: A regional strategic dialogue aligned with the operationalisation of the Arab Peace Initiative (API)

• Number of experts in the region engaged to help identify specific measures that would prompt key regional players to contribute to paving the way towards the resumption of the peace process. • Number of measures and arrangements identified in dialogue with experts in the region. • Number of decision makers with whom the recommendations are shared and with whom ECF actively engaged as reflected in the number of briefing and meetings with these decision makers, feedback and expressions of interest and follow up. To be monitored internally by ECF staff who will track attendance in briefings and meetings, follow-up interactions and expressions of interest, cross-border initiatives etc.

target.value:
Five (5) specific recommendations identified on how to enhance the engagement of key regional players in support of the Israeli-Palestinian peace process based on consultation with Egyptian, Jordanian, European and US experts, including one joint regional workshop.
Active engagement with and dissemination to eight (8) senior decision makers in the region (3 US, 1 Egyptian, 1 Jordanian, 1 Palestinian and 2 Israelis).
Feedbacks received indicating increased understanding of the role regional players can play in facilitating efforts by key regional states in support of the Israeli-Palestinian peace process and incentivising both Israel and the PA to move forward.

actual.value:
ECF, in collaboration with Egyptian, Jordanian and Palestinian experts, drafted 5 policy papers on ways to enhance the engagement of key regional players in support of the Israeli-Palestinian peace process. ECF hosted a workshop with Israeli, Egyptian, Jordanian, US and Palestinian experts on ways to enhance regional engagement in addressing Israeli-Palestinian tensions.
ECF actively engaged with and disseminated policy recommendations to 7 US officials, 2 Egyptian officials, 1 Jordanian officials, 2 Palestinian officials and 2 Israeli officials.
The US State Department provided feedback including a recommendation to engage UAE stakeholders. ESF further met with Israeli officials regarding their recommendations related to the Negev Forum who expressed sincere interest. ECF got feedback from Saudi scholar Dr. Alghashian on "Operationalising the API". ECF gained recommendations from Jordanian, Saudi, Egyptian, UAE, Bahraini participants at a seminar on the POTUS visit.

target.value: Clearer and more substantial understanding of the potential contributions of a regional API-based MEPP. Expanded support for an API-based MEPP in Israel and the region, as a track to be launched in parallel to the IL-PAL peace process and as a means to support and incentivize it.

actual.value: In 2023, ECF concentrated its efforts on defining the Israeli-Palestinian components of a Potential Israel-Saudi Arabia Normalization Deal with Israel to achieve its objective of identifying initiatives expanding the contribution of regional players and stakeholders in support of a two-state solution. To that end, ECF drafted a roadmap outlining the Israeli-Palestinian pillar of a potential Israeli-Saudi normalization deal which was shared and discussed with relevant US stakeholders, including relevant officials from the Department of State, the US National Security Council and the US Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, and also shared with Saudi authorities. ECF’s Palestinian contact discussed the draft with PA advisers to Mahmoud Abbas, Hussein el Sheikh and Majid Faraj. All those who received this draft shared enthusiastic feedback with constructive comments and suggestions Based on the assumption that Saudi Arabia is the main player likely to determine the scope and nature of the Israeli-Palestinian components of a deal, a new draft of the memo was prepared, aimed at explaining to a Saudi audience less familiar with the practical details of the conflict, the rationale behind the proposed roadmap and its various components. In parallel to these efforts, ECF engaged in the development of an Israeli-US-Saudi track II dialogue by initiating ties with the Gulf Research Center, a Saudi think tank.

target.value: One comprehensive set of specific recommendations on the operationalisation of the API Recommendations disseminated to 15 decision makers.

actual.value: Recommendations finalized and shared with 16 key stakeholders defined as the main target groups for the project.

title.narrative: Outcome 1: ECF seeks to create conditions for a successful resumption of an Israeli-Palestinian peace process and the realisation of a viable two-state solution. In order to address the current deadlock that has characterized the Israeli-Palestinian process in the last years, ECF is focusing on identifying and advancing policies at three levels: 1) Changing dynamics on the ground 2) Enhancing regional contribution 3) Strengthening international engagement in the support of TSS.

1) Identified policy measures that Israel, Palestine, regional and international players could undertake in support of the Israeli-Palestinian peace process of Palestinian state building and development and of the Gaza stabilization. 2) Engagement of relevant Israeli, Palestinian, regional, and international stakeholders with the policy recommendations developed by ECF at each of the three levels mentioned above. 3) Israeli-Palestinian agricultural ties formed, based on cooperation, mutual confidence, and common interests.

target.value: Identified uni-, bi-, and multilateral policy measures that IL, PAL, regional, and international players could undertake in support of the MEPP.
